about.title: An orthodontic specialist, not just a dentist who also does braces
body: Ashwin Dental Care was set up around a specific gap in Mugalivakkam — patients who needed real orthodontic expertise, not a general dentist fitting braces on the side.

Dr. Ashwin Kumar, a qualified orthodontist, leads every braces and Invisalign case personally, from the first bite assessment through to retention — while the clinic's general dentistry side handles everything else a family needs, from checkups to root canals.

The clinic sees a mix of teenagers starting orthodontic treatment for the first time and adults choosing Invisalign for a more discreet option, and treatment plans are built around what actually fits each patient's life and budget.

faqs.question: Braces or Invisalign — which is right for me?
faqs.answer: Braces handle more complex bite corrections and don't rely on patient compliance, while Invisalign is more discreet and removable. Dr. Kumar will recommend one based on your specific case during the consultation.

faqs.answer: Most cases take 18–24 months, though this varies with how complex the correction is.

blogPosts.title: Braces or Invisalign? How to Decide What's Right for You
blogPosts.excerpt: Both straighten teeth effectively, but they suit different cases and lifestyles — here's how to think through the choice.
blogPosts.author: Dr. Ashwin Kumar
content: Traditional braces and Invisalign both move teeth into proper alignment, but they get there differently, and the right choice depends on your specific case.

Braces use fixed brackets and wires, giving the orthodontist precise, continuous control over tooth movement — which makes them better suited to complex crowding, large gaps, or significant bite corrections.

Invisalign uses a series of custom, removable clear aligners. It's a strong option for mild to moderate corrections and is popular with adults and image-conscious teens because it's far less visible day to day.

One trade-off to consider: because aligners are removable, results depend on wearing them 20-22 hours a day. Patients who won't reliably keep to that schedule often get better outcomes with fixed braces.

The only way to know for sure is a proper orthodontic assessment — X-rays and a bite analysis will show whether your case is straightforward enough for aligners or needs the control that braces provide.
Whichever option fits, both lead to the same outcome: a straighter, healthier bite. The consultation is where that decision gets made, not before.
